second_order: working out and building the SG banner and logo
theme_note: These codes hold together as the practical work of locating, sizing, staffing, designing, revising, and building the community's marks. What varies is whether a turn recruits labour, settles placement, proposes a design, or adjusts pixels already laid.

second_order: marking one stage finished and moving to the next job
theme_note: These codes announce milestones or a last contribution while treating completion as a stage that can lead into another logo, cleanup, or defence. What varies is whether the marker closes the first build, the banner, or one participant's pixel work.

second_order: watching, repairing and defending the SG/BM murals
theme_note: These codes share the practice of shifting attention and pixels toward whichever adjoining mural needs protection or repair. They vary between watching, raising alarms, requesting help, fixing damage, reporting allies, and narrating attacks.

second_order: making room for neighbours instead of erasing their work
theme_note: These codes hold together as working around neighbouring pictures and requests so the SG work does not start a fight. They vary between warnings, relayed requests, border compromises, refusing interference, and yielding desired space.

second_order: sorting out mistaken help and repairing overwritten art
theme_note: Both exchanges turn apparent obstruction or actual overwriting into identification, apology, stopping, or offers to rebuild. What varies is whether the harm came from misplaced attempts to help SG or from SG pixels covering a neighbour.

second_order: using old alts to speed up pixel work
theme_note: This single code records a distinct way one participant multiplied their available placements; it belongs with no other practice in the pool.

second_order: asking to show the work to SG staff
theme_note: The paired turns hold together as proposing and encouraging a move from making the picture to showing it to the people represented.

second_order: celebrating what the group made and defended
theme_note: The founding code celebrates both communities being represented; later retrospective praise can extend this only where it similarly credits or admires the shared result.

second_order: saving and thanking people for murial timelapses
theme_note: These turns preserve the finished event by sharing a whole timelapse, cutting out the group's portion, and thanking the person who made that view usable. The practice varies between supplying the record, refining it, and acknowledging that work.
regrouped_from: opened in slice 02 after comparison with slice 01; kept separate from celebrating the result because these codes make and acknowledge a viewable record of how it developed

second_order: recounting improvised, avoided, destroyed and remade work
theme_note: These retrospective turns preserve complications beneath the polished ending: starting without a full design, staying out for fear of damage, watching work reform, and remembering local pattern battles. What varies is whether speakers regret, abstain, marvel, or compare memories.
regrouped_from: opened in slice 02 after comparison with slice 01; kept separate from live building and defence because every code is retrospective and foregrounds the imperfect process remembered after closure

second_order: hoping to colour pixels again next April
theme_note: The two-turn exchange converts the finished project into a hope and a suggested date for doing it again.
regrouped_from: opened in slice 02 after comparison with slice 01; kept separate from celebrating this murial because it imagines a future canvas
